items.stem: A team wants to add a feature because an executive likes it, with no user evidence. A Scrum-with-UX approach would first:

options.text: Frame it as a hypothesis and run a small experiment to test the assumption
options.rationale: Correct: assumptions are validated with experiments before large investment.
Large investment before validation is risky.
Input is welcome, but it is tested, not blindly built.
Measuring outcomes is central to the approach.

items.explanation: Correct: assumptions are validated with experiments before large investment.

items.stem: Integrating UX with Scrum means UX work should primarily happen:

options.text: Within the Sprints, collaboratively and iteratively
options.rationale: Correct: UX is integrated into the cadence, not a separate up-front phase.
A big up-front phase contradicts the approach.
Late UX misses the chance to shape the product.

options.text: By a separate team that never meets Developers

items.explanation: Correct: UX is integrated into the cadence, not a separate up-front phase.

items.stem: Which TWO signals indicate a team is genuinely outcome-focused in Scrum with UX? (Select TWO)

options.text: It measures whether users' problems are actually solved
options.rationale: Correct: measuring user outcomes shows outcome focus.

options.text: It validates assumptions with small experiments
options.rationale: Correct: experimentation reflects an outcome mindset.

options.text: It counts features shipped as its main success metric
options.rationale: Feature count is output, not outcome.

options.text: It avoids ever talking to users
It locks the design before any feedback
options.rationale: Locking out feedback is not outcome-focused.

items.explanation: Correct: measuring user outcomes shows outcome focus. Correct: experimentation reflects an outcome mindset.
